stances_toward.note: Under Orban Hungary took the entity's side against the state: Orban hosted Dodik despite the Bosnian arrest warrant (2025), the deputy foreign minister declared support for RS and its president in Banja Luka (Mar 2025), Hungary refused to recognise the verdict and Eximbank lent RS HUF 45bn in 2022; Hungary voted NO on the Srebrenica resolution; yet Hungary keeps the EUFOR deputy command and a reserve company. Péter Magyar's Tisza won on 12 Apr 2026 and Orban lost power; Dodik says he wants to meet Orban 'as soon as possible'. No source on the Magyar government's line toward Banja Luka was found, so 'warming' is an expectation, not a record (confidence C). Not 'neutral': the legacy ties of Fidesz to SNSD remain.

stances_toward.note: The one EU government that has shielded Minsk in Brussels: Hungary blocked a joint EU-member statement condemning the 26 Jan 2025 election, forcing Kallas to speak alone. Partner rather than ally: no treaty, and Hungary is in NATO and the EU, whose sanctions it implements. Single-source and one episode, hence confidence C. Bond - affinity: two leaders at odds with Brussels.

stances_toward.note: Hungary under Orban was Georgian Dream's shield in Brussels: Budapest and Bratislava vetoed EU sanctions on Georgian officials in December 2024. The change of government in Hungary in May 2026 (Magyar) removes that shield, and the EU is reported to return to sanctions; the single source for the 2026 turn is Azerbaijani press, so the trend is a reading (C). Bond affinity: the 'sovereigntist' politics of the two ruling parties.

stances_toward.note: NATO and EU co-member, tied by oil: JANAF carries non-Russian crude to MOL, Hungarian firms hold Krk LNG capacity, and Hungary supplied EUR 3.2bn (7.1%) of Croatia's imports in 2025. Visible friction: the INA-MOL stake dispute that Plenkovic says 'has constrained' relations, Zagreb's refusal in Feb 2026 to pass Russian Druzhba crude to Hungary and Slovakia (EU-backed), and MOL's competition complaint against JANAF (4 Mar 2026). Warming because Peter Magyar, who won the April 2026 election, told Plenkovic at Bled on 31 Aug 2026 he was ready for 'a new chapter' on INA and the two directed their foreign and economy ministers to talk. Reluctant ally rather than partner because both are bound by treaty (NATO, EU) but the business is adversarial. Bond none: interest only.

stances_toward.note: An EU member whose government blocked the opening of Moldova's first cluster for almost two years (a veto aimed at Ukraine, to which Moldova's file is tied) and whose new government lifted it in early June 2026 after an agreement with Kyiv on the Hungarian minority, though it now resists simultaneous opening of the remaining clusters and withheld a joint letter on 17 Jul. Hungary's MET Group is also the buyer of the gas Moldovagaz delivers to Transnistria. Graded partner because the friction is about pace and procedure, not about Moldova's membership; confidence C because the warming rests on a transition of power in Budapest, not on a bilateral act. Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Under Orban, Budapest was VMRO-DPMNE's closest ideological friend in the EU and the lender of EUR 1bn (two government loans, Oct and Dec 2024, 3.25% fixed) that refinanced the January 2025 Eurobond; Hungary also gave Nikola Gruevski asylum in 2018 and refused his extradition in 2019. Orban lost the April 2026 election: Prime Minister Magyar called Gruevski 'a criminal', and on 1 Sep 2026 Hungarian police opened a criminal probe into Eximbank deals including the Skopje loan. Partner, not ally, although both are NATO members; the opposition calls Orban and Vucic Mickoski's mentors. Trend cooling because the personal patron has gone and the loan is under investigation. Bond - affinity: a shared conservative-nationalist camp, which survived the fall of its leader only as a debt.

stances_toward.note: Hungary is an EU member and Ukraine only a candidate, so the 'co-members become reluctant allies' rule does not apply; Hungary has been the most obstructive member state: it held the accession veto for 17 months, blocked clusters 2 and 3 on 17 Jul, 1 Sep and 8 Sep 2026, and opposes a fast-track. Rival, not adversary: Budapest never wished Ukraine's defeat. Warming because the April 2026 election removed Orban and Prime Minister Magyar announced a 'comprehensive agreement' on the rights of about 100,000 ethnic Hungarians in Transcarpathia and lifted the veto on 7 Oct, conditional on Ukraine's education law; relations stay tense (Sybiha-Magyar clash in Sep, the football blacklist). No source uses the word 'rival'; our reading, confidence C. Bond - grievance: the minority question.
